model_annotation: The image presents a line plot illustrating the loss as a function of the number of iterations for five different setups: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128). The x-axis is labeled "#Iteration" and appears to be a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 140,000 iterations. The y-axis is labeled "Loss" and also follows a linear scale, with a range from approximately 2.4 to 3.4. In the plot, each line represents a different setup, differentiated by color and has a distinct marker shape. The "Vanilla" setup is depicted by a solid purple line, "StrmLLM (n=64)" by a solid blue line, "SepLLM (n=64)" by a solid orange line, "SepLLM (n=64, H)" by a solid green line, "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" by a solid red line, and "SepLLM (n=128)" by a solid pink line. All lines start at the same loss value near 3.4 and then rapidly decline, demonstrating a steep decrease in loss early on, followed by a plateau and a more gradual decline. The lines suggest that early iterations are critical for loss reduction and that the loss plateaus and then slowly increases as the number of iterations grows. No explicit data points are provided, but the general trend of each line can be observed from the start to the end of the x-axis.
